headline: Water Level Monitoring and Park Access
reservation: Most public parks around Lake Travis, such as Pace Bend, do not require advance permits for day use, but individual campsites must be reserved through the Lower Colorado River Authority (LCRA). Boat rentals should be secured weeks in advance for summer weekends. Always verify current dock and ramp status on the official LCRA website, as water levels fluctuate significantly.

days.title: Limestone Cliffs and Coves

stops.name: Pace Bend Park
stops.detail: Explore the rugged western shore, famous for high limestone cliffs and deep-water coves suitable for swimming.

stops.name: Mansfield Dam Park
stops.detail: Visit the site of the massive dam that created the lake, offering one of the most accessible public boat ramps.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes; lake geography requires long detours around the water
days.note: Check water levels before planning cliff-side activities; exposed rocks can pose hazards.

days.title: Hill Country Overlooks

stops.name: Balcones Canyonlands National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Hike the Doeskin Ranch trails for panoramic views of the surrounding Texas Hill Country ecosystem.

stops.name: FM 1431 Scenic Drive
stops.detail: Navigate the winding road between Lago Vista and Marble Falls for elevated vistas of the reservoir's north shore.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; winding roads require slower speeds
days.note: Expect high temperatures and limited shade on hiking trails during summer months.

days.title: Marina Life and Sunset Views

stops.name: Cypress Creek Park
stops.detail: A quieter inlet on the north shore ideal for birdwatching and gentle water access.

stops.name: Oasis Bluff
stops.detail: Visit the tiered walkways along the cliffs of the south shore for views of the main lake basin.

days.driving: Allow 30–50 minutes; expect congestion near Austin
days.note: There is no bridge connecting the north and south shores; plan travel accordingly.

intel.title: Ramp Closures
intel.text: Low water levels frequently lead to the closure of public boat ramps. Consult the LCRA daily report to confirm which ramps are currently operational for motorized craft.

intel.title: Township Services
intel.text: Fuel and supplies are readily available in Lakeway and Lago Vista. Marinas offer fuel for boats, but prices typically reflect the convenience of water-side service.

intel.title: Weekend Crowd Management
intel.text: Popular parks like Pace Bend can reach capacity early on Saturdays. Arrive before the peak afternoon window to ensure entry to designated day-use areas.

intel.title: Rural Hill Country Connectivity
intel.text: Signal is strong near Lakeway but can drop significantly within the canyons of Pace Bend Park. Print directions if visiting the more remote western park areas.

intel.title: Heat Awareness
intel.text: Summer temperatures often exceed 100°F. Limit strenuous hiking to the hours before 10 AM and carry more water than typically anticipated.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at Austin-Bergstrom International Airport. Stock up on supplies in Lakeway or Bee Cave before heading to remote lakeside rentals.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is sufficient for most paved roads; check rental terms for driving on unpaved park paths.
plan.goldenHour: The cliffs at Pace Bend Park offer a classic Hill Country sunset, though the specific angle shifts with the seasons.
